title: Alexander Dunne: 'I'll leave nothing on the table' in pursuit of title
excerpt:
It was P2 in the Madrid Feature Race for Alexander Dunne on a good weekend for the Rodin driver

It was a positive weekend in Madrid for Alexander Dunne. The Rodin Motorsport driver made a return to the podium for the first time since Barcelona's Feature Race.

Though the Irishman has achieved four top five finishes and a further four top 10 finishes in that time, it was a good result according to Dunne, as he was pleased with single-lap and race pace all weekend.

"I feel good, I'm very happy," Dunne reflected. "I'm not normally this happy to finish second, so I'll take it while it lasts. I think it was a good weekend. Qualifying was strong, race pace was very strong. I think ultimately Dino did a very good job this weekend, his pace was very strong.

"I think he and I were probably quite a bit quicker than the rest of the grid, so I think in general the pace and that sort of thing was really strong.

"I'm very pleased, I think the team and I made a good step. One that I really hope we can continue to carry forward for the rest of the year. Overall, I think it was a very good weekend."

Dunne was back on the F2 podium and says the team's performance was much more in line with expectations

The Madrid Feature Race was a tricky race strategically, with an early Safety Car leaving many teams and driver split on when to make their mandatory stop.

While Dunne was initially wanting to come in at the first opportunity, so much so he had openly told his team over the radio that was his preference, the Rodin driver ran longer in the end.

It proved to be the correct choice, with another Safety Car providing him and eventual race winner Dino Beganovic the ideal opportunity to pit and emerge without losing track position.

READ MORE

FIA Formula 2 announce supersized Baku Round

Dunne explained the thinking behind those early laps and how the strategy calls evolved in a race that continued to ebb and flow in and out of favour of the title contenders.

"It was really difficult. Ultimately, if there's a Safety Car on Lap 6, you can come in for a free pit stop, but then you also have the possibility of getting stuck behind someone who's slower than you. I think you need to have a massive pace advantage to be able to get past them again.

"Realistically, we made the right decision. I managed the Soft tyre as well, I was able to extend quite long and we got the chance to wait for that second Safety Car.

The Irish driver is still aiming for the F2 title and took a big chunk of points out of leader Tsolov

"If you look at Rafa and Martinius, who were behind me, they had to pit a little bit early to cover off someone who had pitted before them.

"In the end, that kind of destroyed their race. I was considering pitting not too long after they did, but I'm very glad I didn't."

With Baku up next, Dunne's weekend in Madrid closed the gap down to Championship leader Nikola Tsolov. There is still plenty of ground to make up, with 38 points separating the Irish driver in P4 and the points leader.

Round 12 will be a supersized round, with an extra Qualifying and Feature Race providing even more points, and Dunne says he'll be aiming to maximise his chances of catching the Bulgarian.

"I'm pushing hard to try and get at least in the top three. I think it's going to be difficult, but we've been improving at the moment. For sure, as a driver, I'm going to leave nothing on the table, leave it all out there. I think we should end up in a good place."

Next Up

title: Freddie Slater signs with Invicta Racing for 2027 F2 campaign
excerpt:
Freddie Slater will graduate up to FIA Formula 2 next season with Invicta Racing. The team is the first to announce a driver for the 2027 campaign, with the 2026 FIA Formula 3 runner-up joining the current F2 Teams’ Champions.

Slater secured one race victory this season in F3 along with a further seven podium finishes and three pole positions en route to P2 in the Drivers’ Standings.

Prior to F3, the Audi Driver Development Programme talent earned titles in the Formula Regional European Championship in 2025, Italian and UAE F4 titles in 2024 and the Ginetta Junior Championship in 2023.

Slater said that he was eager to begin work with his new team ahead of the 2027 campaign. “I’m really excited to be stepping up to Formula 2 with Invicta Racing next year. I learned a lot in Formula 3 this season, and I feel I have developed as a driver and as a person over the course of the year. Invicta has a great record in Formula 2, and I cannot wait to get started with the team and prepare for our campaign together. I am also very grateful for the continued support from the Audi Driver Development Programme. There is still a lot for me to learn, and I’m really looking forward to taking on this new challenge.”

Invicta Racing CEO and Team Principal James Robinson added: “We’re delighted to welcome Freddie to Invicta Racing for 2027. To finish runner-up in the FIA Formula 3 Championship in his first season is an outstanding achievement, particularly given the level of competition in the category. His results throughout the year, including a victory, three pole positions and eight podiums, underline the pace and consistency he has shown. Freddie has demonstrated that he is ready for the next challenge, and we’re very excited to help him take that next step in Formula 2.”

Allan McNish, Director, Audi Driver Development Programme said: “The move to Formula 2 is the natural next step for Freddie, and an important new phase of his development as a driver. He enjoyed a strong Formula 3 season, fighting for the title until the final round - showing his speed, racecraft and progress throughout the year. We are very proud of what Freddie has achieved this season and how he has developed along the way. Invicta Racing has had an excellent record in recent years, and we are delighted to be working with them. We believe it is the ideal environment for him, and we look forward to supporting him as he takes on this new challenge in 2027.”

title: FIA Formula 2 announce supersized Baku Round
excerpt:
The FIA Formula 2 Championship announce that Round 12 of the F2 2026 season, which will take place on 24-26 September at the Baku City Circuit, will be enhanced, with an additional Qualifying session and a second Feature Race.

The final two rounds of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will resume with the usual weekend format made of one Free Practice followed by one Qualifying, a Sprint Race and a Feature Race.

Bruno Michel, FIA Formula 2 CEO said: “As Formula 2 is the only Support Event at the Azerbaijan Formula 1 Grand Prix, together with the promoters, we have opted for a supersized F2 race weekend, with one Free Practice, two Qualifying sessions, one Sprint Race and two Feature Races.

“This is the only weekend where the Timetable allows the additional sessions, which will increase the level of entertainment even further for the attending crowd and all our fans. The Baku City Circuit always provides us with amazing racing, so we’re very pleased to make the 12th Round of our season pretty unique.

“We will then revert to our usual race weekend format for the final two rounds of the 2026 season, which will be held at Doha and Yas Marina.”

Round 12 schedule will consist of:

Thursday morning: one 45-minute Free Practice session.

Thursday afternoon: two consecutive 20-minute Qualifying sessions.

Friday morning: Sprint Race, with the reverse-grid order determined by the results of the first Qualifying session.

Friday afternoon: First Feature Race, with the starting grid set by the results of the first Qualifying session.

Saturday morning: Second Feature Race, with the grid determined by the results of the second Qualifying session. Pole position in each Qualifying session will award 2 points, while both Feature Races will carry the standard points allocation, including 1 point for Fastest Lap, providing they are in the top 10 positions of the final race classification, in accordance with the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

title: Round 11 Post-Feature Race Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Welcome, everyone, to today’s FIA Formula 2 Press Conference following the Feature Race here in Madrid. Joining us is Ritomo Miyata of Hitech in third, Alexander Dunne of Rodin Motorsport in second, and Dino Beganovic of DAMS Lucas Oil, who has claimed his first Feature Race victory in Formula 2. Congratulations, Dino. A dominant victory and your first Feature Race win. How does that feel?

Dino Beganovic: It obviously feels very good. It has been a while and I feel like we have been waiting for this one for a long time. It feels very good to get it here after a very good Friday.

FIA Formula 2: You looked completely dialled in. Tell us about the car the team gave you this weekend.

Beganovic: Honestly, the team did a good job all week. We came from the simulator having tested some things and went in a direction they had not been used to before, but it obviously worked this weekend. Hopefully, we can carry it on to Baku. From Free Practice, I felt very good and confident in the car, and that is all you need at this track.

FIA Formula 2: You started on the soft tyre. How did it hold up during your first stint?

Beganovic: Honestly, the soft tyre was very good today and yesterday. It was very fast and the grip was solid. At the start of the race, we were quite slow and tried to remain flexible with what we could do. Once the first few drivers pitted, we knew what to do. We picked up our pace and were able to match them and then go quicker, which was a good sign. Everything went to plan and the Safety Car was a bonus for us.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on the victory. Alex, congratulations on P2. Can you take us through your race?

Alexander Dunne: I think it was a good one and I am very happy. The Soft tyre had quite a lot of performance, more than I expected, even with how strong it looked in the Sprint Race yesterday. Most of the drivers who used it yesterday gained places and maintained them, whereas I expected the tyre to degrade a little more towards the end. The performance of the soft tyre, our first tyre today, helped Dino and me finish where we did. We were able to extend the first stint for a long time and wait for a Safety Car. Even without one, if you had asked me to do another 10 laps at the same level of performance, I think I could have done it. I was impressed by how good the soft tyres felt. They degraded to a certain point and then did not get any worse. The lap times stayed consistent. That was the key to having a good race today.

FIA Formula 2: Were you able to use the Hard tyre and push a little more towards the end of the race?

Dunne: Definitely a little. For whatever reason, it was much more physical on the hard tyre. Physicality and steering weight were things we discussed coming into the weekend, and particularly today because the race was 10 laps longer than yesterday. On the soft tyre, it was not too difficult, but on the hard tyre it was really tough. The steering weight through Turn 12 and all the high-speed corners was very demanding. At the end, I had to back off because, if I had pushed slightly over the limit, I do not think I would have been able to catch the car because the steering was so heavy. We need to understand why it felt so different between the soft and hard tyres. The pace was still very strong and we managed to set the fastest lap as well, which was good.

FIA Formula 2: Describe the physicality of the race. Through La Monumental, it looked as though you were pulling some very high G-forces.

Dunne: It was crazy. I saw a video the other day saying that the corner is more than 500 metres long. We go through there at over 200 kilometres per hour and there is a lot of banking, which naturally puts much more load through the car. It is also where we have the most downforce, so the steering becomes really heavy. It was pretty tough. At the end, I had to back off a little through Turn 12 because it was too difficult and not worth risking an incident. Up to that point, I think we got the most out of it.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on P2, Alex. Ritomo, congratulations. Hitech appeared to give you a very good car this weekend. How did it feel?

Ritomo Miyata: It is amazing to be back on the podium. We finished P3 after starting P9. The strategy was good and the Safety Car helped us gain positions, but we also had good pace. That is why we are here.

FIA Formula 2: How physically challenging was it for you today?

Miyata: Turn 12 and the banking were definitely very tough. The steering feedback was heavy. I came from Super Formula, where they have power steering, so Formula 2 has much heavier steering and is physically demanding. Today was very different compared with yesterday. The prime stint was very tough physically.

FIA Formula 2: How was the tyre degradation over the race distance?

Miyata: The tyre degradation was quite flat and not too high, but Turn 12 became much more physically demanding. It was difficult to drive on the limit because, if you pushed too much, the car could slide and feel unpredictable, and it was difficult to add steering input because it was so heavy. I tried to stay just under the limit there and then push in Sectors 1 and 3.

title: FEATURE RACE: Dominant Beganovic takes lights-to-flag victory in Madrid
excerpt:
Dino Beganovic was in a league of his own in Madrid, leading every lap to win Sunday’s Feature Race by over seven seconds.

The DAMS Lucas Oil driver converted pole into a 7.3s victory over Rodin Motorsport’s Alexander Dunne, while Hitech’s Ritomo Miyata followed up his Sprint Race success with another podium in third.

AS IT HAPPENED

It was a great start from pole for Beganovic, while Dunne retained P2 ahead of Rafael Câmara, despite locking up into Turn 1.

Behind them, Nikola Tsolov, who was the lead driver to start on the Hard tyre, was sitting in fifth but coming under pressure from Roman Bilinski.

The Safety Car was signalled with Kush Maini in the barrier at Turn 18 after a collision with Cian Shields. The AIX Racing driver was given a 10-second time penalty for his part in the incident.

Racing resumed on Lap 7 with TRIDENT bringing Laurens van Hoepen into the pitlane from P8. Mari Boya and Van Amersfoort Racing duo Nico Varrone and Rafael Villagómez also came in for their mandatory stop.

Noel León then got past Bilinski for P6 at Turn 1, while Gabriele Minì dived to the inside of teammate Oliver Goethe for ninth at Turn 13.

The Italian attempted the same move on Miyata on Lap 10 but ran too deep, allowing the Hitech driver to retain eighth.

At the end of the next lap, León was the first of the front runners to come into the pitlane. He put on the Hard tyre and lost out to Boya, who was flying on the softs, at the exit.

The Mexican driver then went side-by-side with John Bennett through La Monumental but kept the position.

Câmara was next to come in and changed to the Hard tyre, but Boya was flying on the softs and overtook the Invicta Racing driver at Turn 13.

Stenshorne and Tsolov were in from P4 and P5 on Lap 14, and while the Rodin driver stayed ahead, the Bulgarian lost out to Boya, although he was able to fire up his Soft tyres to overcut Câmara.

Oliver Goethe was next to pit from P8 and came out right in front of Boya and Tsolov, just as they were fighting for position. As they went three-wide into Turn 5, the Campos driver ran off track, but as he filtered out, he lost the place to Câmara.

Boya then made his way past the MP driver at La Monumental, with Câmara now sizing up a move on Goethe.

The two went side-by-side through Turn 1 at the start of Lap 18 but Goethe wound up in the barrier at the exit of Turn 2. This brought out the Safety Car while Câmara was given a 10-second time penalty.

At the same time, Bennett pulled over to the side of the road with an issue with the marshals also having to clear his TRIDENT.

This stoppage allowed the drivers who had not pitted to come in for their mandatory stop, with Beganovic, Dunne, Miyata, Emerson Fittipaldi, Joshua Duerksen and Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak all gaining an advantage and making up the top six positions ahead of Stenshorne.

Racing resumed on Lap 22 of 32 as Beganovic started to pull away from Dunne. Minì made a move past Stenshorne for seventh, once again at his favoured Turn 15.

Câmara was keen to get a move on and went past Boya with the help of DRS into Turn 5, while Tsolov followed him through on the next lap.

The race was now running to time and with just under seven minutes, Dunne brought the gap to Beganovic down to one second, but the Swede responded with the fastest lap to extend the lead to 2.2s.

Further behind them, Fittipaldi was holding on to P4 as Duerksen put him under pressure. The Paraguayan tried a move at Turn 15, but the AIX driver held on.

Tsolov then lost P10 to Bilinski, with the DAMS driver using the DRS to get ahead into Turn 5. Duerksen’s pressure on Fittipaldi finally told with Invicta making a neat move on the brakes into Turn 13.

Tsolov’s day was going from bad to worse as he lost more places to Boya, León, van Hoepen and Montoya all overtaking him on the penultimate lap.

But out in front, Beganovic was in supreme form, winning for the first time this season. Dunne was second ahead of Miyata, with Duerksen in P4. Fittipaldi held on to fifth ahead of Inthraphuvasak, Minì and Stenshorne. Câmara’s penalty dropped him to P10 with Bilinski in ninth.

KEY QUOTE – Dino Beganovic, DAMS Lucas Oil

“Winners in Madrid, it feels amazing. From pole position, a great weekend, very good pace. I want to thank the team for the amazing car all weekend, especially the bounce back from Monza. Super happy with this and now we look forward to Baku.”

CHAMPIONSHIP STANDINGS

Nikola Tsolov continues to lead the way on 177 points, with Rafael Câmara seven points behind in second. Gabriele Minì is third on 153 points, with Alexander Dunne on 139 in fourth, Noel León fifth on 119.

In the Teams’ Standings, Campos Racing lead the way on 296 points, with Invicta Racing second with 260. Rodin Motorsport are third on 209, with MP Motorsport fourth on 190, as ART Grand Prix round out the top five on 159 points.

UP NEXT

Next up for the drivers is a trip to Baku for Round 12 of the 2026 season from September 24-26.

title: Colton Herta withdraws from Madrid Feature Race
excerpt:
Hitech has confirmed that Colton Herta will not take part in the FIA Formula 2 Feature Race in Madrid.

The American did not compete in yesterday’s Sprint Race and will not race on Sunday.

A Hitech statement said: “Colton will not be racing today after continuing to feel unwell."

Drivers that were set to start behind Car 4 on the Feature Race grid will move up one position each on the grid.

title: Round 11 Post-Sprint Race Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 2 Press Conference following the Sprint Race in Madrid. Joining us are P3 from Trident, Laurens van Hoepen, P2 from AIX Racing, Emerson Fittipaldi, and from Hitech, claiming his first Formula 2 victory, Ritomo Miyata. Ritomo, congratulations on the victory. How does that one feel?

Ritomo Miyata: I am really happy. Finally we won a race because we have struggled during the season. To finally win is a really good feeling.

FIA Formula 2: Take me through the start because you had a great one.

Miyata: I was expecting an overtake opportunity at the start, so I really focused on the launch. We managed the race well from there.

FIA Formula 2: It is the first win for Hitech since Baku last year. Tell me about the car they gave you today.

Miyata: This year I expected much more, but during the season we struggled, especially on short-run performance. We analysed everything during the summer break and finally came back with strong performance. That is why we won today, and since Monza we have been back to our level.

FIA Formula 2: Emerson, congratulations on P2 and your first Formula 2 podium. How does that feel?

Emerson Fittipaldi: It feels great to be on the podium in Formula 2 in my rookie season. Doing it with AIX is incredible. We have worked hard all season through a lot of challenges and difficulties. It is always rewarding to stand on the podium after all that effort.

FIA Formula 2: Laurens was chasing you at the end. How hard was it to hold him off?

Fittipaldi: It was quite tough. The car was not easy to drive and I was struggling quite a lot, but I kept it on the track and managed to finish P2.

FIA Formula 2: You started on the Hard tyre. How was the degradation?

Fittipaldi: This track is very demanding on the tyres because it has high-speed, medium-speed and low-speed corners. It is a tough circuit and I think tomorrow will be a great race as well.

FIA Formula 2: Laurens, congratulations on P3. Can you take me through your move on Noel?

Laurens van Hoepen: The start was not great, but after that we had good pace, partly because of the compound we were on. I knew I had to make the move at some point. Overtaking is very difficult here, so I prepared it as much as possible and when I saw my chance I went for it. It worked out well and it was a calculated move.

FIA Formula 2: Talk us through the closing laps when you were behind Emerson.

Van Hoepen: It is hard to follow on this track because overtaking opportunities are limited. I was trying to pressure him into a mistake, but my tyres were fading as well. I got close a few times but it was not enough.

FIA Formula 2: You started on the Soft tyre. Did you know it would remain competitive for the whole race?

Van Hoepen: That was the plan. We hoped it would be a little stronger at the start and maybe weaker at the end, but the performance stayed quite similar throughout the race. That was positive, although it is a shame we could not make more of it.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on P3.

title: Kush Maini handed grid penalty for Madrid Feature Race
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of Saturday's FIA Formula 2 Sprint Race in Madrid, Kush Maini has received a penalty.

During the Sprint, the ART Grand Prix driver made contact with Van Amersfoort Racing’s Nico Varrone at Turn 8.

After the race, the Stewards heard from both drivers and their team representatives and examined video evidence, onboard footage and GPS data. They determined that Car 16 was wholly to blame for the collision.

Maini therefore has been awarded a 10-second time penalty, which is converted into a grid drop of five positions in accordance with Article 39.3(b) of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

Maini is set to start from the back of the grid in Sunday’s Feature Race.

title: SPRINT RACE: Miyata eases away to claim maiden victory in Madrid
excerpt:
Ritomo Miyata put in an assured performance to claim his maiden FIA Formula 2 victory in the first ever Madrid Sprint Race.

The Hitech driver seized the lead of the line and then managed two Safety Car restarts expertly to take the win. AIX Racing’s Emerson Fittipaldi achieved his first podium in second ahead of TRIDENT’s Laurens van Hoepen.

AS IT HAPPENED

Miyata had a great start and took the lead before Turn 1 ahead of Fittipaldi. Noel León held on to P3 ahead of van Hoepen who, alongside Gabriele Minì and Mari Boya, started on the Soft tyres, while the rest chose Hards.

There were plenty of battles, as Rafael Câmara overtook Dino Beganovic for seventh at Turn 5 while Alexander Dunne dived to the inside of Roman Bilinski for P8 at Turn 8.

The Safety Car was called upon at the end of the lap. Kush Maini and Nico Varrone had contact at Turn 7 which sent the Van Amersfoort Racing driver spinning into the barrier.

Elsewhere, Sebastián Montoya and John Bennett collided at the opening corner. Both drivers came back into the pitlane, and while the former continued on, the latter retired with damage.

Racing resumed on Lap 5 of 23 with Dunne looking to make a move. The Rodin Motorsport driver went to the outside of Câmara at Turn 5, but his Invicta Racing rival held on.

The Irishman tried the same move on the next lap but again found the door shut.

Further ahead, van Hoepen was keen to make his tyre advantage count, and the TRIDENT driver dived to the inside of León at Turn 13 but could not make it stick.

Van Hoepen then dived to the inside of León at the Turn 5 chicane on Lap 9. The Campos driver reclaimed the position at Turn 8, but having gone off track, he was told to give the place back to the TRIDENT a couple of laps later.

León was struggling and his teammate Tsolov tried to take advantage with a move past at Turn 1 on Lap 13. He held him off, but their fighting was bringing Martinius Stenshorne, Câmara, Dunne and Boya into the mix.

Fittipaldi had closed to within 1.1s of Miyata, but Van Hoepen was almost half a second quicker, as he set the fastest lap of the race.

Tsolov, having been on the radio calling for Campos to let him go and catch van Hoepen, tried a move at Turn 5. But as he went off track to get ahead, the Bulgarian gave León back the place.

Unfortunately for the Red Bull Junior, his day was over a few corners later. A slight brush with the wall at Turn 20 spun him into a stoppage, bringing out the Safety Car.

With Tsolov’s car cleared, Miyata led the field to green on Lap 18, with van Hoepen immediately putting Fittipaldi under pressure.

The Hitech driver was in good form, having pulled out a 1.3s lead and set the fastest lap of the race.

Van Hoepen had DRS and was within 0.3s of Fittipaldi on Lap 20, but the Brazilian was doing well to hold on to P2.

Miyata however was in a league of his own, driving away from the rest to win by 2.6s – giving Hitech their first victory since the 2025 Baku Sprint Race.

Fittipaldi held on to second ahead of van Hoepen, with León in fourth ahead of Stenshorne. Câmara kept Dunne in his mirrors for sixth, while Boya took the final point in eighth.

KEY QUOTE – Ritomo Miyata, Hitech

“Finally we have won a race. Thanks to Hitech, Morizo-san, and Toyota Gazoo Racing, who have always supported my career, and also thanks to my family, my girlfriend, and my fans. We achieved a win in an F2 race. But we have another race tomorrow, so we need to do our best, so see you tomorrow.”

CHAMPIONSHIP STANDINGS

Nikola Tsolov continues to lead the Drivers’ Standings on 177 points, with Rafael Câmara in second on 169. Gabriele Minì is third on 147, ahead of Alexander Dunne is on 120 points, with Noel León a further point behind in fifth.

Campos Racing top the Standings on 296 points, as Invicta Racing sit second on 247. Rodin Motorsport are third on 186 points, just two points ahead of MP Motorsport, with ART Grand Prix in fifth on 151.

UP NEXT

The drivers have one more chance to claim victory in Madrid, as they will return on Sunday morning for the Feature Race. Lights out is set for 11:25 local time.

title: Colton Herta withdraws from Madrid Sprint Race
excerpt:
Hitech’s Colton Herta will not take part in the Madrid Sprint Race.

Car 4 was worked on during the Restricted Period without an approved exception, breaching Article 21.6 a of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

As a result, Car 4 was set to start the Sprint Race from the pit lane as per Article 37.2 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

However, Hitech has confirmed Herta's withdrawal from Saturday's race.

Drivers set to start behind Car 4 on the grid will move up one position each.

title: Several drivers given permission to start both races in Madrid
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of the FIA Formula 2 Qualifying session in Madrid, several drivers have lost their fastest laptimes and received permission to start both the Sprint and Feature Races in Madrid.

Firstly, Nico Varrone has lost his fastest time from Qualifying. The Van Amersfoort Racing driver was determined by the Stewards to have been the sole cause of the second Red Flag, a breach of Article 33.5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

With the deletion of his fastest time, was left without a time within 107%. In accordance with Article 34.2 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations, the VAR driver has been given permission to start both races from the back of the grid.

The Van Amersfoort driver is set to start the Sprint from 19th.

Secondly, Kush Maini has lost his quickest time from the session after being the sole cause of the first Red Flag, breaching Article 33.5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

As a result, the Indian driver was left without a laptime within 107%. In accordance with Article 34.2 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations, the ART Grand Prix driver has been given permission to start both the Sprint and Feature Races from the back of the grid.

The ART driver is set to start the Sprint from 20th on the grid.

Thirdly, Sebastiàn Montoya has been given permission to start both races in Madrid.

The PREMA Racing driver failed to set a time within 107%, however, as per Article 34.2 of the Sporting Regulations, has been permitted to start from the back of the grid.

Montoya is set to start the Sprint Race in Madrid from P21.

Finally, Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak has been given permission to start both races in Madrid.

The ART driver did not take part in Qualifying and subsequently had no time within 107%. As per Article 34.2, the Thai driver has been permitted to start both races from the back of the grid.

Inthraphuvasak is set to start from P22 on the Sprint Race grid.

title: Fittipaldi ready to capitalise on best F2 Qualifying result in Madrid
excerpt:
Emerson Fittipaldi secured P10 in the FIA Formula 2 Qualifying session in Madrid, a season-best result for the AIX Racing driver.

The Brazilian left it late in the day but kept his cool under pressure having had an earlier laptime deleted for exceeding track limits.

Reflecting on his session back in the paddock, Fittipaldi explained just how difficult the session was to manage from the cockpit.

"I'm very, very happy. I can only thank God for this result. It was a very stressful and chaotic qualifying as everybody saw.

"It's a very technical and difficult track and finally we got the car in the window where we could be competitive and in the top 10 and that's amazing.

"Because no one's been here before, I think that really helped level things out. Most of the other races this season, it was my first time there when all the others had already raced there, so that has been a big disadvantage.

"Today was very fair and the team managed to give me a very nice car and finally we have a top 10 and reverse pole tomorrow, so it's an amazing weekend already."

Diving deeper into his session, Fittipaldi explained how his qualifying session took shape, with the AIX driver losing an earlier effort to a track limits violation.

Along with that, the three Red Flag stoppages meant that there was no time to get into a rhythm during the half-hour session, and that it all came down to that final lap.

"Up until the last push of the whole qualifying session, I didn't have a lap in," Fittipaldi explained. "I was dead last, so it was very, very stressful. I got track limits and red flags here and there and you're like, 'oh my God, what am I going to do now?'

"Then in the last lap, I was like, let me give it everything I have and that was enough to put me in top 10, so that was good."

Looking ahead to the remainder of the Madrid weekend, Fittipaldi is aiming to capitalise on his strong grid position for both races.

Overtaking is set to be tricky according to the drivers, meaning that reverse grid pole potentially holds even more value around the Madring.

The AIX driver isn't getting carried away however, and is focused on executing a clean weekend from here on out.

"Hoping for the best result possible. I don't want to add any extra pressure, just enjoy starting from the front row and do the best I can.

"I know that the team will give me the best car that they can do because the engineers have been working so hard this year and we've been working so much to try to develop and improve to be closer to the top teams. Finally, now we're getting there.

"I think it's going to happen mostly off the line, that's where most people are going to get their overtakes done. I'm in a pretty good position, I think, for tomorrow's race because it's a track where you really cannot overtake easily and it's very challenging.

"I'll just do the best race I can tomorrow and see where we finish."

title: Round 11 Post-Qualifying Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA FORMULA 2: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 2 Press Conference following Qualifying here in Madrid. Joining us in P3 from Invicta Racing, Rafael Câmara. In second place from Rodin Motorsport, Alexander Dunne; and from DAMS Lucas Oil, taking his third pole position in Formula 2, Dino Beganovic. Congratulations, Dino. How does that one feel?

DINO BEGANOVIC: It feels amazing to do it here in Madrid and to be the first one to do it here. Obviously, we did not get many laps in Free Practice, so that put a lot of emphasis on being well prepared for Qualifying through all the simulator work we did at the factory. I think we did a very good job. The car was really good today and DAMS did a great job to come back very strongly after a disappointing weekend last week in Monza. It feels very good.

FIA FORMULA 2: With the Free Practice running that you did have, how challenging was it to get the car properly set up for qualifying?

BEGANOVIC: I think the main thing is having trust between the engineer and the driver at that point, because the engineers cannot read much from the data and the drivers are still learning. You cannot learn much from an engineering perspective. My engineer and I dug into it a little and, in the end, we just tried to make me as comfortable as possible going into Qualifying. I think we did the right thing.

FIA FORMULA 2: This was the first Formula 2 Qualifying session here in Madrid. What did you make of the circuit?

BEGANOVIC: It is a crazy track. It brings the heart rate up very quickly, especially on a qualifying lap. It will also be very tough on the tyres in the races and physically hard on the drivers. I think we have some exciting races ahead, but tomorrow we will have to focus on gathering data for Sunday.

FIA FORMULA 2: Congratulations on pole position, Dino. Alex, congratulations on P2. Can you take us through your session?

ALEXANDER DUNNE: I think it was pretty good. It was a messy session because we had so many red flags, but one good thing for us was that we were at the front of the pit lane. We were first out, or one of the first out, each time, which is definitely useful in a qualifying session like this. I have qualified second and third many times, so pole would have been nice. But, considering how difficult the session was, I am pretty happy to have put together a clean lap and finished in the top three.

FIA FORMULA 2: Was it easy to get the tyre into the operating window, or did it take some coaxing to bring it in?

DUNNE: Today it was quite easy because of the red flags. We never really went out on a brand-new set and had the chance to build them up before pushing. We were always on fresh or used tyres, so they had already been through a heat cycle and were ready when we started to push. I did not even do a warm-up lap before my final lap and the tyre was already ready. If we had all gone out on new tyres after the final red flag, I imagine we would have struggled more, but because we had completed so many laps in between, it was not too bad.

FIA FORMULA 2: What are your initial thoughts on the track?

DUNNE: It is pretty cool. I had a few scary moments at the beginning of Free Practice, but it was much calmer and more relaxed in qualifying. It is definitely one of the more physical tracks. Of all the tracks I have driven so far in Formula 2, this will probably be the most physically demanding, and the Feature Race is a long one as well. I will need to make sure I am well prepared for that.

FIA FORMULA 2: Well done on P2, Alex. Rafa, congratulations, it looked like quite a final lap from you. What was it like in the car?

RAFAEL CÂMARA: It was not an easy Qualifying session. It was tricky to get the laps in, with a lot of red flags and crashes. I think there was one mistake on my side and, without that, the lap could have put us in a more comfortable position. I did not risk too much on the last lap, but overall I am happy with what we did today. In the end, it was a good lap that put us in P3. From here, we focus on the races.

FIA FORMULA 2: As I asked Dino, was it a challenge to get the car into a good setup window, or did you find it quite straightforward?

CÂMARA: It was not easy in Free Practice because we did not get many laps. It was difficult to get a read on what we needed to do for Qualifying, so you had to trust your engineer and the team to move in the right direction. Overall, it was a good Qualifying session without much data from Free Practice. That was the same for everyone, but on a new track it is not what you want. You want to have a good read and go into Qualifying knowing more about what is going to happen. It all came down to the final lap, which was very important because otherwise we would have been outside the top 10. We can be happy with what we did today.

FIA FORMULA 2: What are your initial thoughts on the track? Did you enjoy qualifying here?

CÂMARA: It is not an easy track, and it is quite easy to make a mistake, especially on a new circuit where there is not much grip or rubber. From a drivers' point of view, it is very nice. You need to be committed and confident on the lap. If you think too much about the mistakes you could make, you can end up making one. It was an intense qualifying session on a nice track.

title: QUALIFYING: Beganovic storms to pole around Madring
excerpt:
Dino Beganovic was in superb form to earn the Aramco Pole Position Award, his first since the opening round of the 2026 campaign.

The DAMS Lucas Oil driver was a consistent presence at the top of the times, delivering a 1:44.331 to take the first ever FIA Formula 2 pole in Madrid. He beat Alexander Dunne and Rafael Câmara to top spot.

On the first set of push laps, ART Grand Prix's Kush Maini suffered a spin ahead of Turn 15 and hit the wall to bring out the Red Flags.

In a separate incident, Sebastiàn Montoya tagged the barriers in his PREMA Racing car to sustain suspension damage. Maini was out of his car and OK while the Colombian recovered to pit lane entry.

The session resumed with 23 minutes remaining, and everyone eager to record a banker lap.

Nikola Tsolov was the early pacesetter, going quickest on a 1:46.328 for Campos Racing, with Dunne P2 for Rodin Motorsport, 0.002s down on the leading effort.

The second Red Flag arrived as Nico Varrone found the barrier at Turn 18 in the Van Amersfoort Racing #22. He was out of the car and OK, but everyone else returned to the pit lane while his car was recovered.

Running resumed with 18 minutes left on the clock and once again, there was a rush to get another lap in.

Dunne took top spot by almost a full second as the track continued to improve. TRIDENT's Laurens van Hoepen went up to P2 nearly eight tenths off top spot.

Beganovic then delivered a 1:45.182 to secure P1 by 0.2s over Dunne, with teammate Roman Bilinski going third-fastest with little over 11 minutes remaining.

The Swede found another chunk of time with eight minutes to go, setting a 1:44.578 to extend his advantage to eight-tenths of a second over his closest challenger in Dunne.

A third Red Flag arrived with just over five minutes remaining, with John Bennett in the barriers. The TRIDENT driver was OK, but his car needed clearing from Turn 11.

Running resumed once more with 05:28 on the clock and time for one last run.

Personal best sectors were flying in, and Dunne pipped Beganovic to take top spot briefly until the Swede finished his latest lap, lowering the time to beat to a 1:44.331.

Despite a big oversteer moment at the final corner, Invicta Racing's Câmara jumped up to third having been outside the top 10 prior to crossing the line.

Stenshorne and Tsolov set identical times, however with the Rodin driver completing his first, he lined up fourth ahead of the Championship leader.

There was one final incident, with Colton Herta spinning at Turn 19 into the barriers to leave everyone else unable to improve.

It left Roman Bilinski sixth ahead of van Hoepen, Noel León, Ritomo Miyata, with Emerson Fittipaldi completing the top 10.

The FIA Formula 2 Sprint Race is set to get underway on Saturday afternoon at 14:00 local time.

title: Nikola Tsolov: 'So far so good' after topping Madrid Practice
excerpt:
It was a positive start to the Madrid weekend for Nikola Tsolov, with the Championship leader topping Practice and what was FIA Formula 2's first session around the Madring.

The Campos Racing driver was consistently at or near the top of the timing sheets in what was a heavily impacted session following a Red Flag.

However, the Bulgarian driver was enthusiastic about his and the team's chances heading into the important Qualifying hour, and Tsolov says he is optimistic of a fight for pole.

"A very chaotic session, just like we were expecting. But I think I felt confident from the get-go in the car and confident with the track, so I was always there.

"It was all about putting the lap in at the right time, really. So I expect a lot to change for Qualifying obviously different compounds, but it's a good start and I'm happy with how we're working so far."

The Red Bull Junior Team driver also touched on Campos' preparation for the weekend, with the F2 team leaning on their F3 counterparts following a two-day test around the Madring last month.

Having data to analyse and compare to was hugely beneficial says Tsolov, who added that it meant the team wasn't starting from zero this weekend.

"F3 has been quite useful to us to check on-boards and obviously all the car-related stuff, set-up, bumps, all those things that are new to you when you jump in the car. At least you know some of those kinds of things.

"I think we've been working quite closely with the F3 team and that has been a benefit to us."

Looking ahead to Qualifying, the Campos driver said that the grid would encounter an entirely different track in terms of conditions.

The temperatures will be higher, while the switch to Soft tyres will give the drivers extra grip and confidence, which he believes could lead to further excursions as drivers find the limits.

"I think I'll take a similar approach. We expect a big jump in grip, so I'm definitely going to be pushing more in quali and then adapting to whatever the condition is in the session because as we saw, I think there's going to be a lot of offs and Red Flags probably.

"The last couple of rounds haven't been easiest with penalties and things like that, so I'm just trying to get back on track as soon as we can.

"I've done the last three races with penalties consecutively. So, I'm trying to get back on track and quali is important here.

"Looking forward to having a bit more of a positive weekend and heading with better momentum into the final part of the year."
